hypothesis: KDA stage 2 reaches every logical chunk through a runtime start offset: it pads the packed time axis, materializes each BT tile with a vmapped dynamic_slice, and scatter-adds the kernel outputs back through an [NC, BT] int32 position vector. chunk_kda_fwd always hands that stage a varlen-aligned layout in which chunk c is exactly rows [c*BT, (c+1)*BT), so a contiguous chunk-block schedule can re-block it by reshape: no tile copy, no int32 position vector, no T+BT scatter buffer. That removes the DMA-bound index/copy segments the campaign attributes to kda-long while returning bit-identical tensors.

estimate.reasoning: The aggregate objective is 3.349ms (tiny-linear-serving is the only model with a plan; the dense/MoE callsites are deferred). The action's two affected callsites are 50.5% of it: kda-long 1.133ms = 33.8% and kda-short 0.560ms = 16.7%. UPPER BOUND from the campaign L1 panel: 35% of kda-long sits in two int32 index segments (#47 22% + #42 13%, cmp=0%/bw=100%) and 11% more in a float32 rank-3 segment -- exactly the pos/flat_pos position vectors and the per-chunk gather/scatter tile copies. Stage 2 owns roughly half that machinery (stage 2 issues 5 gathers + 4 live scatter-adds, stage 4 issues 4 gathers + 1), i.e. ~23% of kda-long, giving 0.338*23 + 0.167*12 = 9.8%. LOWER BOUND from a full 420-configuration timing sweep of both KDA cases on this round's GPU-interpret proxy: the best deployable config improves from 0.9998ms to 0.9556ms (4.42%) on kda-long and from 0.4110ms to 0.4054ms (1.36%) on kda-short -- both at the unchanged incumbent knob settings -- i.e. 0.338*4.42 + 0.167*1.36 = 1.7%. That denominator is inflated because every Pallas stage runs interpreted here, while the deleted work (about 18MB of HBM traffic per kda-long call -- the T+BT pads, the per-chunk gather copies and the zero-initialized scatter buffers -- plus 9 dynamic-index operations) is unchanged by interpretation. The estimate takes a conservative 8% local relief on kda-long and 4% on kda-short, inside those bounds: 0.338*8 + 0.167*4 = 2.7 + 0.7 = 3.4%.

hypothesis: The GLA recurrent-state stage launches its Pallas grid as (H, K/BK, V/BV, NT) and only the chunk axis is sequential -- the head axis is pure parallelism that carries no data between programs. Every head therefore pays a full program prologue, grid bookkeeping, boundary-scalar read (chunk_to_seq, bos, eos, seq_real_lens) and its own narrow k/v tile transfer to run one [BK,BT]x[BT,BV] state update. A head-grouped schedule gives one program HEAD_GROUP adjacent heads, each keeping its own recurrent scratch plane and its own unchanged arithmetic, so the boundary scalars are read once per group and the k/v tiles arrive as one wider transfer instead of HEAD_GROUP separate ones. Head arithmetic is never mixed, so the emitted per-head states and final states are the incumbent's.

estimate.reasoning: The paired incumbent aggregate is 3.358ms and tiny-linear-serving is the only model with a plan. The action's two affected callsites are 53.2% of it: gla-long 1.097ms = 32.7% and gla-short 0.689ms = 20.5%. LOCALIZATION: a stage decomposition of the incumbent-selected plans on this round's GPU-interpret proxy puts chunk_fwd_h_kernel_varlen at 0.537ms of gla-long's 1.082ms (49.7%) and 0.514ms of gla-short's 0.693ms (74.2%) -- the single largest stage at both callsites, and the stage this action schedules. A grid-program scaling sweep isolates the cause: state-stage latency is 58-89us per grid program and is flat in tile size (H=8,T=2048,cs=2048 -> 8 programs -> 0.555ms; H=8,T=512,cs=512 -> 8 programs -> 0.501ms; H=1 -> 1 program -> 0.089ms at both shapes), i.e. the stage is per-program overhead bound, not work bound. Grouping G heads per program divides the program count by G, so the relief is a schedule property rather than an arithmetic saving. MEASURED UPPER REFERENCE: a full 2x112-configuration deployable sweep of both GLA cases on the proxy takes the best deployable config from 1.0091ms to 0.8151ms on gla-long (19.22%, both at chunk_size=2048/compact_alignment=True/output_value_tiles=4) and from 0.6279ms to 0.5008ms on gla-short (20.25%, chunk_size=512/compact_alignment=True/output_value_tiles=8), i.e. 0.327*19.22 + 0.205*20.25 = 6.3 + 4.2 = 10.4% aggregate; all 224 configurations stayed correct. That denominator is inflated for the target: the interpret proxy pays a Python-level grid loop per program, so it exaggerates the fixed per-program cost that Mosaic amortizes in hardware. The estimate discounts the measured local relief by roughly 40% to 11% on gla-long and 12% on gla-short, which are still above the residual grid/prologue cost a real Pallas launch pays per program: 0.327*11 + 0.205*12 = 3.6 + 2.5 = 6.0%.

hypothesis: The GLA output stage is the only stage that both owns the intra-chunk score tile and owns the layout its rows are finally read in, and the incumbent schedule is pessimal on both counts. It materializes one chunk-wide BT x BT fp32 score tile per output tile -- 16 MiB at BT=2048, roughly half of it masked away again -- so its score arithmetic AND its elementwise decay/mask traffic grow with the square of chunk_size; and it returns the aligned staging layout, leaving the caller to restore token order with a read-modify-write scatter over the ALIGNED index space, which touches every output row through an accumulate. A resident output schedule fixes both: the chunk is walked in fixed-height sub-chunks whose own rows need only a (128,128) score tile while every older row of the same chunk arrives through a running (K,V) state -- exactly how a chunk already reads preceding chunks through h -- and the stage lands its rows directly in token order, expressing the identical permutation over the OUTPUT index space so each row is moved exactly once. The sub-chunk axis stays a batch dimension of single contractions and the state recurrence is resolved as one (num_sub, num_sub) decay matrix, so the operation count is unchanged while every operand shrinks. Nothing is dropped or approximated: it is the same linear-attention sum re-associated, and the restored layout is bitwise identical to the scatter's.

estimate.reasoning: SHARE: the paired incumbent aggregate is 25.601ms and the action's two affected callsites are 64.2% of it -- gla-long 12.853ms = 50.2% and gla-short 3.574ms = 14.0%. hypothesis: Every chunk-blocked KDA stage reaches its chunks through a RUNTIME start offset, even though the entry has already made that offset a compile-time constant. Stage 2 over-allocates the packed time axis by BT, materializes each chunk's q/k/gk/beta/v tile with a vmapped dynamic slice, and returns its five live results by scatter-accumulating them through an [NC, BT] int32 position vector into zero-initialized T+BT-row staging buffers; stage 4 then re-gathers that staging layout one chunk at a time to read stage 2's Aqk back, scatters its own rows into another staging buffer, and hands the result to a fori_loop-built un-align gather. But chunk_kda_fwd aligns every sequence to a multiple of the state block, which is a multiple of BT, so logical chunk c is EXACTLY rows [c*BT, (c+1)*BT) of the packed layout: the chunk axis is a static reshape of the time axis and the entire index space is redundant. The variant blocks and un-blocks by that reshape on both sides of the stage-2 -> stage-4 handoff, so the chunk-blocked results never leave the layout the launch produced them in -- the reshape and its inverse annihilate and the aligned staging buffers are never materialized at all. Neither side alone suffices, which is the whole point: whichever end keeps its index-space addressing pins the layout and forces the round trip, so removing only stage 2's scatter is worth 0.17% and removing only stage 4's is worth 0.57%, while removing both is worth 75%. Nothing is approximated or dropped: each result row is written exactly once instead of accumulated into a zeroed buffer, and the emitted tensors are BITWISE identical to the incumbent's on both compared outputs -- verified not only on the gate's single-sequence canonical inputs but on five ragged multi-sequence packed batches (2 and 3 sequences, lengths that force real alignment padding, chunk_size 16/32/64/128, state_block_chunks 1/2/4), every one of which matches the frozen pure-JAX recurrence and agrees with the incumbent to 0.0 on both the token output and the final recurrent state.

estimate.reasoning: SHARE: the paired incumbent aggregate is 10.580ms and tiny-linear-serving is 100% of the three-model total, so the action's two affected callsites are 89.9% of it -- kda-long 6.296ms = 59.5% and kda-short 3.221ms = 30.4%. That scatter/gather machinery is the campaign's named LIMITER (kda-long -> #47 jit|int32r2, cmp=0%/bw=100%, DMA memory-bound -- cut bytes moved / keep data resident), and this action's source function is the stage that produces its input. MEASURED: at each callsite's DP-selected incumbent plan -- kda-long cs=128/ibs=16/cbc=1/sbc=2/sda=128 and kda-short cs=64/ibs=8/scalar=True/cbc=2/sbc=2/sda=64 -- the full chunk_kda_fwd pipeline goes from 6.0892ms to 1.5171ms (75.09%) on kda-long and from 3.0455ms to 0.3953ms (87.02%) on kda-short, with both compared outputs (token output and final recurrent state) bitwise equal to the incumbent's and both inside the frozen reference tolerance. Even crediting ONLY the separately measured single-stage effects and none of the cancellation -- 0.57% on kda-long and 1.52% on kda-short -- the bar is cleared at 0.595*0.57 + 0.304*1.52 = 0.8%, which is why the round is proposed on the combined schedule rather than on either half; the combined form is what the 71.1% above measures.
